**Not in this slice:**

## Why

The plan, the spec check and the spec draft flag a backticked Check entry whose first word cannot run. They skip any entry whose first word is a path listed in Files (`internal/engine/brief.go:788`, `checkCommandWarnings`). That skip also covers directories and plain source files that already exist. A Check entry such as `internal/cli` therefore passes the gate. The slice checks then fail with "executable file not found", which is the failure S563 was meant to stop. The reviewer raised this in round 1 of ork run ork-20261125-163301-8662 for S563, and S563 left it out of scope. The exemption should cover only a Files path that does not exist yet, so a script the slice will create can still be named in Check. An existing Files path falls through to the normal rule: it must be found on PATH, or be an executable regular file in the worktree.

Two related defects from the same S563 run are fixed here, as the owner chose (session 8d711f67, 2026-11-25).
- (b) `ork run --questions` and `ork wave start --questions` exit 3 (`ExitWaitQuestion`) for an item held only by a Check finding, although it has no question to answer. Owner decision adj 568 (`cli.questions-check-finding-exit`): skip. These items now give `ExitOK` and print the `held: ITEM: LINE` line. `ExitWaitQuestion` stays for items with real owner questions.
- (c) The TUI joins an item ID and a Check finding with a space, giving "S90 Check entry ...". It should use "S90: " as the CLI does. An adj wait note keeps its wording, "B waits on adj 42".

## Implement

1. In `internal/engine/brief.go`, change `checkCommandWarnings`. Replace `if paths[strings.TrimPrefix(word.text, "./")] { continue }` with a check that also requires `filesPathNotYet(word.text, worktree)`. A path listed in Files is exempt only when it is relative, stays inside the worktree after `filepath.Join` and `filepath.Rel`, and `os.Lstat(filepath.Join(worktree, path))` fails with `errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist)`. Any other Lstat result (exists, or another error) is not exempt. The entry then goes through the existing PATH and executable-file lookups, so an existing executable regular file in the worktree still passes. Add `errors` and `io/fs` imports if they are missing.
2. Update the comment on `SliceCheckCommandWarnings` or `checkCommandWarnings` to say that a Files path is exempt only while it does not exist.
3. In `internal/cli/wave.go`, change the `if len(open) > 0 { return nil, nil, ExitWaitQuestion }` branch after the `--questions` listing. Return `ExitWaitQuestion` only when some item in `open` is not held only by a Check finding. Such an item is one with `len(r.Findings) > 0`, no `Questions` and no `WaitsOn`. Items that wait on adj, and items with questions, keep today's exit 3. When every `open` item is held only by a Check finding, return `ExitOK` and skip the `no open spec questions` line. The `held: ITEM: LINE` lines were already printed above. The exits at 705 and 735 concern real questions and stay.
4. In `internal/tui/speccheck.go`, add a helper `heldNote(id string, r daemon.SpecItemResult) string`. It returns `id + ": " + specNote(r)` when `len(r.Findings) > 0`, and `id + " " + specNote(r)` otherwise. Use it in `heldNotes` (line 406) and in both status strings in `finishLaunchSpec` (`internal/tui/launch.go:378` and `:380`).
5. Tests: add and change the tests listed above, red before the code and green after. Run `go test ./internal/tui -update` only if a golden changes, and review its diff. None should change, because no golden holds a Check finding.
6. Docs. In `docs/design.md`, reword the exemption at 3318-3319 to say an entry whose command word matches a Files path is exempt only when that path does not exist in the worktree (or the checkout before the worktree exists), ignoring line anchors and a leading `./`. Reword the exit text at 3078 so the `--questions` listing exits 3 only with questions pending, and 0 for an item held only by a Check finding. Make the same two edits in `docs/guide.md` at 518 and 618-620: "paths listed in Files that do not exist yet are exempt".
7. Run `slicer note` and the changelog step as `slicer ai instructions` directs: `slicer changelog add S572 --text "..."`.
